CAPTURE.meaning: Retain a candidate need and its source/authority status without treating receipt as approval.
CAPTURE.entry: Identifiable source proposal, decision or existing requirement with provenance.
CAPTURE.actor: Existing intake/operator authority; deterministic inventory records facts, product authority resolves admission.
CAPTURE.operation: Identify and deduplicate against existing owners; preserve immutable source and distinguish reference, definition, retirement and unresolved authority.
CAPTURE.output: Source-linked candidate identity, ownership/overlap disposition and authority status.
CAPTURE.exit_gate: A canonical authorized requirement or explicitly flagged in-scope authored draft can enter SPECIFY; unsupported proposals remain candidates.
CAPTURE.failure: Conflicting or absent authority is recorded for decision; no BIU or scheduling assignment is inferred.
CAPTURE.evidence: Pinned source, identity/overlap decision and admission attribution.
CAPTURE.visible_state: Existing CAPTURE semantics; no product-intake automation or Project edits implied.

SPECIFY.meaning: Close intent, value, scope, exclusions and feasible acceptance/evidence meaning before design.
SPECIFY.entry: Identified in-scope requirement and authoritative source revisions.
SPECIFY.actor: Requirement analyst under existing product authority; Founder resolves product gaps and ratifies newly authored definitions.
SPECIFY.operation: Write the eleven fields, distinguish selected/rejected candidates, expose amendment dependencies and resolve ambiguity through attributed decisions.
SPECIFY.output: Versioned requirement specification, feasible acceptance predicates and explicit authority-gap disposition.
SPECIFY.exit_gate: No unanswered product meaning is delegated to design. A ratification-pending specification may support explicitly conditional candidate design, but cannot be represented as adopted authority or execution-ready.
SPECIFY.failure: Unresolved intent returns to clarification; excluded pending extensions cannot leak into selected scope.
SPECIFY.evidence: Specification revision, authority references, ambiguity decisions and acceptance-feasibility review.

DESIGN.meaning: Close architecture, interfaces, trust, persistence, failure/recovery and verification decisions through a proportionate Design Contract and independent Design Verification.
DESIGN.entry: Specified product meaning, with any conditional ratification clearly visible.
DESIGN.actor: Designer followed by mechanical checks and an independent design reviewer; product questions return to their authority.
DESIGN.operation: In a later authorized phase, prepare the contract, verify conformance/premises, and separate fixed decisions from implementation-local freedom.
DESIGN.output: Identifiable Design Contract plus mechanical and independent verification results.
DESIGN.exit_gate: Required decisions closed, conformance and feasible proof accepted, unresolved authority surfaced; no BIU decomposition bypasses this gate.
DESIGN.failure: Failed premise or authority conflict holds affected design; material revisions require re-verification.
DESIGN.evidence: Design revision, fixed/deferred decision inventory, premise evidence and independent findings.
DESIGN.visible_state: Semantic sub-stage/gate within SPECIFY/PLAN per SWF-25; not a new visible Project lane. This phase does not write a Design Contract.

PLAN.meaning: Arrange approved requirements and verified design into bounded deliverable extents and a coherent dependency plan.
PLAN.entry: Specified requirements and approved verified design, with explicit authority for the planned scope.
PLAN.actor: Planning authority prepares the dependency/coverage plan; Founder resolves scope, scheduling or decomposition changes outside delegation.
PLAN.operation: Allocate intent and proof coverage, identify prerequisite predicates and capability/budget constraints, validate the DAG without inventing priority.
PLAN.output: Versioned decomposition plan and requirement/obligation coverage graph.
PLAN.exit_gate: No orphan obligations, unresolved endpoints or cycles; plan respects fixed design and authority. Existing-decomposition revisions require separate approved split/replan authority.
PLAN.failure: Unowned scope or infeasible dependency returns to SPECIFY/DESIGN or a planning decision; no automatic readiness.
PLAN.evidence: Source/design links, coverage manifest, graph and validation result.
PLAN.visible_state: Existing PLAN; no pending SF-REQ-013 amendment enacted.

TASKS.meaning: Materialize bounded BIU contract candidates from the authorized plan and prepare them for readiness assessment.
TASKS.entry: Approved bounded decomposition and verified design references.
TASKS.actor: Compiler/contract author and deterministic lint; Agent-Ready is the separate readiness assessor.
TASKS.operation: Populate SF-REQ-010 contract duties, fixed decisions, baseline, dependency predicates, capabilities/budgets, candidate custody and pre-implementation verification/evidence obligations.
TASKS.output: Identifiable BIU contracts, lint findings and assessment input manifest.
TASKS.exit_gate: Complete current contracts with resolved boundaries, authority, dependencies and design verification can be assessed; TASKS itself authorizes no implementation.
TASKS.failure: Missing/ambiguous fields hold assessment/admission; changed contract invalidates applicability of prior assessment without deleting it.
TASKS.evidence: Contract revisions, source/design/plan linkage, lint results and assessment lineage.
TASKS.visible_state: Existing TASKS; no worker contracts are changed by this specification.

READY.meaning: An applicable Agent-Ready assessment establishes preparedness, separate from execution release.
READY.entry: Current complete BIU contract with required verified design and an attributable fresh READY assessment.
READY.actor: Agent-Ready assesses; canonical release policy separately evaluates authorization, baseline, dependencies and WIP.
READY.operation: Bind readiness to exact assessed inputs. Retain non-READY outcomes and failed attempts distinctly. Invalidate applicability on material changes and obtain a fresh assessment.
READY.output: Readiness record plus a separate admission/release eligibility result.
READY.exit_gate: IMPLEMENT requires applicable READY plus SF-REQ-002 admission and release policy, satisfied lifecycle dependencies, capabilities and capacity. No manual Project edit can grant execution authority.
READY.failure: BLOCKED, NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, SPLIT_RECOMMENDED, stale verdict or failed attempt holds affected work and routes the appropriate decision/reassessment.
READY.evidence: Immutable assessment, input revision, separate release/baseline record and refusal reasons.
READY.visible_state: Existing READY; preparedness is not execution authorization.

shared_contracts.architecture_scope: All named groups are existing Python src/alienintent modules. The legacy bounded_context field records implementation location; FD-02 does not promote these modules to independent bounded contexts. Proposed module/service/command names below are design targets, not claims of existing APIs. Node remains frozen bootstrap authority; no Node adapter/import dependency or sovereignty claim. Existing canonical-architecture.md separates upstream planning from execution; this design accepts authorized definitions and introduces no general planning or requirements-authoring engine. SF-REQ-013 initial decomposition is distinct from general planning; its allocation-source gap returns to SPECIFY, not to implementers.
shared_contracts.alternatives_and_selection: Select existing SQLite OperationalStore + separate immutable local evidence, instead of a new service/database or a Git-edited canonical requirement register. This preserves transactional recovery and source authority with fewer mechanisms. Withdraw the mandatory supplied-allocation selection: Phase 8 authorizes initial compilation from requirements/design, not validation of hand-authored BIUs. See R1-GAP-013-ALLOCATION; no decomposition mechanism is authorized by this repair. Select fenced durable effect reuse instead of status-toggle/watch-process deduplication.
shared_contracts.value_contract: New internal ports use frozen Python dataclasses/typed enums and standard-library primitives; serialization schema_version=1 is internal only. Required fields described per contract are mandatory; unknown schema version is SchemaIncompatible, missing referenced authority yields Hold. Ref is (project/profile, logical_id, revision_digest, source locator); Result variants are explicit, never bool success. Existing BiuContract and Agent-Ready external schemas are not replaced.
shared_contracts.canonical_encoding: Canonical digest encoding follows BiuContract: UTF-8 JSON, sorted object keys, compact separators; set-valued collections sorted, sequence-valued collections retain order, no NaN/Infinity. Use sha256:<hex>. Raw external evidence also retains a separate exact-byte digest. UUIDs for attempts/episodes are allocated once at ingress and persisted before dispatch; clock/ID creation only at injected composition boundaries.
shared_contracts.evidence_storage: EvidenceRepository is a port owned by evidence_learning; local adapter stores immutable objects under configured external evidence_root/objects/<sha256>. Write temporary sibling, flush/fsync, atomically install without overwrite, fsync directory, verify digest, then CAS operational reference. Crash before pointer leaves harmless unreferenced artifact; crash after pointer is read-verified. No operational commit references unwritten evidence. Distinct namespaces and access labels separate normative refs, observation bodies and verdicts. All referenced history retained in this wave; no GC/retention automation or new learned-policy store.
shared_contracts.operational_storage: Reuse SQLiteOperationalStore and existing profile-scoped versioned aggregate APIs; upstream:<kind>:<identity>, episode:<objective>, attention:<identity> are new namespaced payloads, not a new engine. schema_version in every new payload; reject incompatible version without mutation. Operational pointer writes use CAS; immutable evidence is never updated in place. Future payload migration requires explicit versioned design and is not implementer freedom.
shared_contracts.composition_graph: evidence_profile builds EvidenceRepository. upstream_profile builds inventory -> ambiguity/proof/design admission -> compilation -> readiness consumer. Proof planning depends on design premise inputs, while final verified design depends on proof feasibility: a draft may be inspected both ways, but final applicability pins both artifact revisions; no recursive auto-approval. control_plane_profile builds attention/context/episode/liveness around existing FactoryCoordinator and store. offline_profile assembles the same applications with local external-system adapters. Installation configuration is read only by composition; domain services receive values/ports.
shared_contracts.cross_contract_cycles: 011 and 016 share neutral Ref values, not mutual application imports. 014 creates proof plans from candidate design/premises, 051 reviews that exact pair, 013 consumes the verified pair. 053 exposes AttentionPort independently of 056; 056 consumes it and produces ordinary observed events. Ratification of 056 is required only for 056-specific recovery capability, not for generic 053 attention/tenure.
shared_contracts.failure_protocol: Typed Hold includes reason code, affected refs, evidence refs and required authority/action. StoreUnavailable/SchemaIncompatible stop dependent mutations. VersionConflict never changes an old result to fit new state. No auto-retry may exceed existing authorized budget; failed evidence writes prevent admission. Commands propagate nonzero failure, with held/unverified distinctly rendered.
shared_contracts.interfaces_and_wiring_proof: Every new adapter declares its port; every public composed operation needs intact success and a typed-failure probe against a real temporary SQLite store. LRN-002 is the single reused composition promotion. Static architecture rules do not substitute for runtime reachability or consumer truth.
shared_contracts.authority_boundaries: All ten are design candidates, not release authority. SF-REQ-056 remains AUTHORED_IN_THIS_PHASE and unratified. G1/G2 owner assignment is a real upstream authority prerequisite, not a decision left to implementation. Existing unresolved authority stays explicit even though deferred_to_implementation is empty. No retroactive Wave 1 changes or current worker/lifecycle contract edits. R1-GAP-039-ORCHESTRATION and R1-GAP-039-REAL-OUTCOME block shared-kernel/real-worker changes; R1-GAP-013-ALLOCATION blocks initial compiler decomposition; R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST blocks operational monitor/scan adoption. These are SPECIFY returns, not deferred implementation choices, approved requirements, or authority granted by this design. Unaffected design remains reviewable. R2-GAP-051-EDGE-AUTHORITY is a Founder question about adoption of the R1 module-direction proposal, not a new requirement or reopening of FD-02; normative direction-dependent admission is held, while established architecture checks remain active.
shared_contracts.amendments: POSTW1-DECIDE-007A pending SF-REQ-008, 022, 013, adjacent 025 and 029 are not assumed. Initial compilation excludes general replan; reconciliation excludes new exhaustion/retry policy; episode/effect records use existing store primitives; evidence does not promote learning; telemetry normalization remains outside. Therefore no selected contract requires adoption of a pending amendment. If any is adopted, affected design revisions need independent review before use.
shared_contracts.enforcement_counting: Count each contract opportunity entry once; promotion reuse count is entries with phase3_promotion. Repeated LRN-002 entries are distinct consumer probes under the same promotion, not new controls. Seven unique promotions are reused. All opportunities are proposed, not deployed or proven by this design phase.

atomic_fencing_extension.owner: execution_coordination; proposed FencedOperationalStore port extends existing OperationalStore without replacing it. SQLite adapter uses the same database and existing aggregates/reservations/effects tables. This is design of existing crash-safe semantics, not adoption of pending SF-REQ-008 elaboration.
methods: commit_guarded(profile, aggregate, expected_version, expected_vector, reservations, state, effect_id, payload) -> new_version: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; verify all relevant aggregate versions and exact reservation owner/fences; reject expired episode/authority ref; perform aggregate update and unique effect insertion in the same transaction; commit.

claim_guarded(profile, effect_id, reservations, expected_vector) -> Effect: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; validate all fences and applicable version vector, pending effect and suppression; atomically claim pending to unknown/sending using existing effect status semantics. Duplicate claim is refused.
confirm_guarded(profile, effect_id, reservations, receipt_ref) -> confirmation: validate fence and correlated receipt before existing confirmation transition.
atomic_fencing_extension.boundary: Existing commit_with_effect/claim_effect do not validate a passed reservation fence. They must not be described as sufficient for the new fenced admission. New guarded operations are the mandatory path for episode/liveness effects; old callers remain compatible, but every caller participating in the same episode/lane is routed through guarded operations.
atomic_fencing_extension.dispatch: Reservation is held from intent through send and readback; do not steal/release it solely on timeout. A consumer validates the invocation/effect/fence before accepting a side effect, deduplicates on effect identity and persists its acceptance/outcome. If consumer cannot fence, use exclusive reservation with no reassignment until correlated completion or independently confirmed process death; ambiguity parks. Releasing reservation while an old sender may still act is forbidden. Local effect consumer journal admission serializes with guarded claim; arbitrary remote exactly-once guarantees are not assumed.
atomic_fencing_extension.crash: No live-sender lease expiry or unfenced takeover. Unknown effects read back first. Recovery may confirm original outcome under explicitly validated recovery ownership; stale sender cannot confirm under a released fence. If sender death/outcome cannot be established, retain hold and reservation until authorized resolution.
atomic_fencing_extension.lock_order: For multiple required reservations acquire sorted (profile,scope,key) order; on contention release only reservations newly acquired by that attempt in reverse order and return capacity hold. Never release a retained unknown-effect owner to make progress.

shared_contracts.input_limits: Composition enforces maximum 10 MiB per imported source/evidence JSON object and 256 source documents per inventory request; exceeding limits returns INPUT_LIMIT_HOLD with the offending identity, never truncation or omitted obligations. Paths must resolve within declared permitted roots; UTF-8/JSON decode failure is typed invalid input. Limits are explicit profile policy overrides recorded in the input manifest; changing them cannot change authority.

context_dependency_direction.status: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY; normative module-direction authority unresolved under R2-GAP-051-EDGE-AUTHORITY.
context_dependency_direction.scope: Observation covers every tracked src/alienintent/**/*.py at baseline_commit, including AST Import/ImportFrom nodes under TYPE_CHECKING and re-export statements. Graph keys are internal module groups, not newly approved bounded contexts. Cross-group absolute alienintent imports are aggregated; no relative cross-group imports were observed. This is a source-import snapshot, not runtime/dynamic-import reachability or permission to add edges. Composition-time data flow is not an import edge.
context_dependency_direction.counting: Four importing-file violations, containing five import statements and three distinct module-pair edges. These violate the withdrawn R1 table, not an established product boundary. All five statements are named; no silent exemption.

withdrawn_r1_proposal.status: Historical candidate only; not an allowed-import policy. No implementation or enforcement authority. Any adoption requires a Founder decision and a reviewed design with an executable scope/baseline/expiry predicate.
withdrawn_r1_proposal.target_layers: Outside composition, listed cross-context imports target domain values or ports only, never another context application or adapters. Within a context domain imports domain only; ports import domain/ports; application imports domain/ports/application; adapters may implement ports and invoke applications. Domain/application never import adapters; no context imports composition. Existing architecture layering/vendor/configuration/determinism rules also apply. Composition alone may construct applications/adapters across contexts.
withdrawn_r1_proposal.typed_cycles: execution_coordination MAY depend on context_assembly.domain DesignApplicability values through a consumer port; context_assembly MAY depend on execution_coordination.domain BiuContract and ports. These reciprocal context edges permit leaf type references, not cyclic module imports or recursive application calls. Cross-imported value modules must not import back into their consumers. Port arguments reference leaf values; protocols and adapters depend on those leaves, not vice versa. No new shared context is introduced.

context_dependency_direction.premise_bridge: evidence_learning adapters MUST NOT import installation or composition. composition/upstream_profile constructs an adapter implementing evidence_learning PremiseEvidence, invokes the authorized installation doctor/probe callable at that outer boundary, and passes immutable evidence_learning values inward. composition/doctor_probes is reachable only by composition wiring; no inward import of the composition root. Recorded offline observations use the same port. This remains the proposed Wave 2 composition wiring, not evidence that the withdrawn repository-wide edge table is authoritative.
context_dependency_direction.fitness: 051-architecture-boundary retains BLOCKING existing architecture checks repository-wide using tools/fitness/check_architecture.py --root src/alienintent --check all. It must not compare production imports to withdrawn_r1_proposal. For the proposed directional extension, authority status is explicit: without a pinned Founder disposition of R2-GAP-051-EDGE-AUTHORITY return ARCHITECTURE_AUTHORITY_HOLD for affected design admission, never PASS or an empty successful check. The descriptive graph may be regenerated as observation but cannot authorize or reject product imports. Existing approved checks continue independently. No change to the current checker is claimed here.
context_dependency_direction.conditional_probes: The prior R1 direction/leaf-cycle negative and positive fixtures are retained as conditional candidate-policy tests only, blocked pending Founder disposition and reviewed scope. They cannot certify production conformance or require retroactive source edits. Existing layering/vendor/configuration/determinism checks and composed interface compatibility probes remain unconditional.

monitor_liveness.observation_owner: control_plane owns durable MonitorHealth values and read-only health inspection; execution_coordination owns scan-progress observation. Host/supervisor operational owner remains unassigned, returned to SPECIFY.
monitor_liveness.record: MonitorHealth(profile, instance_id, generation, policy_digest, started_at, last_monitor_tick, last_scan_started_at, last_scan_completed_at, last_scan_outcome, next_scan_due, last_error). Persist monitor ticks independently of whether work exists; scan completion advances only after a full attempt, retaining EvidenceHold/error as outcome. Restart uses new instance/generation and preserves old observations.
monitor_liveness.health_rule: With valid progressing observation clock, no record -> UNVERIFIED; age since last monitor tick > 2*I or overdue last scan completion > 2*I -> STALE; failed/incomplete latest scan -> DEGRADED; otherwise HEALTHY. At exactly 2*I still within bound. Clock regression or unreadable health store -> UNVERIFIED, never healthy. I is the configured scan interval (default 60 seconds for 053 monitor-only operation too). Health is separate from workload quiet/no-gap.
monitor_liveness.supervision: An independently running authorized host observer must inspect health and alert/restart under its assigned policy; self-heartbeats alone cannot detect a dead host. Until the hosting gap closes, expose read-only inspection and make no live supervision/G+I guarantee. No shell background waiter is adopted.

contracts.title: Requirements IR
contracts.domain_owner: Requirements IR domain in context_assembly; source decision issuers retain normative ownership.

ubiquitous_language.RequirementId: Exact supplied identifier satisfying the pinned requirement grammar and authorized namespace; never generated from wording, sort position or encounter order.
ubiquitous_language.DefinitionRevision: Authorized source revision plus normalized semantic digest.
ubiquitous_language.Inventory: Derived view, never a second normative register.

ports: RequirementSource.read(manifest) -> tuple[SourceDocument | SourceUnavailable]; manifest fixes repository/source identity, revision, path, digest, locator and access label.

RequirementInventory.assemble(documents, authority_records) -> InventorySnapshot; resolve(id, revision) -> Definition | Conflict | Unresolved. Inputs/outputs are immutable context_assembly domain values. InventorySnapshot includes typed identifier_issues under identifier_contract; resolve cannot hide malformed tokens as absent.
EvidenceRepository stores snapshot and source manifest; OperationalStore holds current snapshot pointer by expected version.
adapters: Proposed context_assembly/adapters/versioned_source.py reads supplied local files or Git blobs at explicit revisions, with separate parsers for factory-plan headings, Canonical requirement prose and Recorded as prose. It does not crawl or execute imported text.

Proposed context_assembly/adapters/inventory_repository.py binds inventory ports to existing OperationalStore and evidence_learning EvidenceRepository; approved-source manifest provides authority precedence, never file order.
contracts.state: InventorySnapshot: schema_version, source_manifest_digest, definitions indexed by (requirement_id, revision), references, conflicts, unresolved IDs, retired/superseded IDs, dependency edges, BIU satisfaction-link references, prior_snapshot. Each definition has typed SF-REQ-016 role and authority reference. IdentifierShapeConflict records retain raw token, reason, source locator and grammar revision separately from valid-but-undefined IDs.
transitions: PINNED_INPUT -> ASSEMBLED when every readable source is classified; unreadable sources remain UNVERIFIED in a partial snapshot.
Conflicting effective definitions -> CONFLICT for that ID; undefined mention -> UNRESOLVED; approved unambiguous definition -> ELIGIBLE_FOR_PREPARATION. Retirement is preserved, not ID deletion.
A changed semantic or authority revision publishes a new snapshot and marks dependent design/compilation/readiness references stale; old satisfaction observations stay historical.
contracts.identities: Requirement identity is the exact supplied requirement ID (case-sensitive; no prefix rewrite, suffix stripping or zero-padding) scoped to the source project. Revision digest uses canonical JSON of semantic fields and authority revision, excluding formatting/locator aliases. Equivalent formats with the same authority revision merge provenance into one revision; genuinely distinct decisions do not collapse. Snapshot identity hashes sorted source manifest and revision keys.
contracts.persistence: Use the existing execution_coordination.ports.operational_store.OperationalStore, backed by SQLiteOperationalStore; profile-scoped aggregates and expected-version commit. Immutable artifact bodies use the shared EvidenceRepository described in shared_contracts, outside the repository. No new database engine or distributed queue. Inventory bodies and histories are immutable evidence; the current pointer is reconstructible and confers no authority.
contracts.concurrency: Reads return a version; each mutation supplies expected_version. SQLite transactions serialize commits; VersionConflict returns a typed stale-input hold, with no blind retry of a decision. Duplicate identity with identical digest is a no-op; different digest is a conflict. Never hold a SQLite transaction across filesystem, provider or network calls.

identifier_contract.meaning: ASCII, full-token match. One or more uppercase namespace segments, literal -REQ-, at least three ASCII digits, optional single uppercase suffix. SF-REQ-011, SF-REQ-011A, SF-REQ-1000 and TEAM-X-REQ-011 are syntactically recognized. Recognition confers no authority: the pinned approved-source manifest must authorize the exact namespace/project binding; otherwise UNVERIFIED/UNAUTHORIZED_REQUIREMENT_NAMESPACE.
identifier_contract.extraction: Within manifested spans, capture whole heading/Canonical requirement:/Recorded as identifier slots before validation; tokenize reference prose with Markdown-aware delimiters (paired emphasis/backticks/brackets, link labels separate from URLs, terminal prose punctuation). Preserve raw bytes and locator. Classify whole tokens by token_kinds before requirement grammar validation; no conforming substring may rescue an unknown token. A definition slot requires exactly one RequirementIdentifier; empty/ambiguous slots remain typed issues. An AcceptanceCriterionId or CompoundReference in a definition slot is WRONG_IDENTIFIER_KIND, not malformed requirement syntax. Outside declared spans, no requirement-shape issue is emitted; excluded material is not counted as parsed requirements.
identifier_contract.typed_failure: InventorySnapshot.identifier_issues retains IdentifierShapeConflict(status=UNVERIFIED, reason=UNRECOGNIZED_REQUIREMENT_ID, raw_token, source_ref, locator, grammar_revision=2) only for unrecognized tokens in declared requirement/reference spans. Missing/ambiguous slots use MISSING_REQUIREMENT_ID/AMBIGUOUS_REQUIREMENT_ID; wrong-kind definition slots use WRONG_IDENTIFIER_KIND; unauthorized namespace uses UNAUTHORIZED_REQUIREMENT_NAMESPACE. Preserve exact bytes/digest. These block compilation dependent on the affected source spans/IDs, not unrelated sources. Valid undefined requirement references are UNRESOLVED. Recognized acceptance IDs and valid compound/possessive references do not create shape conflicts. Ledger every in-scope token containing -REQ- with its category or issue so omissions cannot pass.
identifier_contract.biu_distinction: Requirement and BIU identifiers are distinct. Wave 1 proposed BIU grammar (docs/evidence/wave1-biu-split-replan-design.json, identity_grammar; not an implemented validator) is \A(?:(?:PG|PY)-[0-9]{2}|WO-[0-9]{6})(?:[A-Z])?\Z. Preserve exact identities, including suffixes; neither grammar allocates identity from sorting or ordinal position. No requirements or BIUs are created by parser fixtures.
identifier_contract.corpus_scope: RequirementSource accepts an explicit versioned source manifest, never an implicit docs/** scan. Each entry pins repository, revision, path, SHA-256, parser form, definition spans, reference spans, namespace/project authority and access label. Only declared spans are requirement-identifier input. Requirements IR production inputs need authorized-source bindings; historical_fixture_manifest below is a read-only regression fixture, not current normative authority. Evidence/reports/prompts/work packets and acceptance/design documents are excluded unless separately manifested with their role and spans; inclusion never promotes observations to definitions. Missing/digest-mismatched source -> SourceUnavailable/UNVERIFIED, not a smaller successful inventory.

token_kinds.acceptance_disposition: Full-token AcceptanceCriterionId is classified before RequirementIdentifier; retain exact acceptance ID and its syntactic parent ID as a typed relationship, never a requirement definition or IdentifierShapeConflict. Namespace/authority and parent resolution are separate from syntactic recognition. No requirement reference is invented merely by stripping the AC suffix.
token_kinds.compound_reference: Reference spans recognize slash lists of full RequirementIdentifier operands (SF-REQ-001/SF-REQ-002), or one full operand followed by slash-separated numeric operands with at least three digits and optional one uppercase suffix (SF-REQ-030/054). Shorthand inherits only the first namespace-REQ- prefix, preserving numeric spelling. Ranges use ASCII .., en dash U+2013 or ASCII hyphen between a full start and full or numeric end (SF-REQ-001–010). Range endpoints must share namespace and digit width, have no letter suffix, and be ascending. Classify as CompoundReference; retain expression and exact endpoints/list operands, never create definitions or identities for unmentioned intermediate values. No range expansion is implied.
token_kinds.unrecognized: In manifested requirement/reference spans, an otherwise unrecognized whole token containing -REQ- remains IdentifierShapeConflict; malformed suffixes SF-REQ-011AA and SF-REQ-011-extra are not compounds. Missing/ambiguous definition slots and unknown namespaces remain blocking typed issues. Unknown acceptance suffix or malformed compound remains a typed issue, never a salvaged prefix.
token_kinds.order: AcceptanceCriterionId, full RequirementIdentifier, fully matched CompoundReference, fully matched PossessiveReference, then typed failure. Category recognition confers no source authority.
token_kinds.possessive_reference: Reference spans recognize a full RequirementIdentifier followed by ASCII apostrophe-s or U+2019-s as PossessiveReference (for example SF-REQ-007's). Retain the raw expression and the exact parent requirement reference; this named whole-expression production is not arbitrary suffix stripping. Definition slots reject it as WRONG_IDENTIFIER_KIND. Other apostrophe suffixes are not accepted.

contracts.state: Immutable AssessmentAttempt includes attempt ID, raw digest, authority/provider/invocation IDs, input fingerprint, predecessor assessment ref, observed disposition or failure, and lint report. contracts.title: Definition / Observation / Verdict separation
contracts.domain_owner: Evidence domain owns typed provenance and linkage. execution_coordination/domain/verdict.py retains execution acceptance policy.

ubiquitous_language.Definition: Versioned normative statement with issuer authority.
ubiquitous_language.Observation: Measured or reported fact with source and scope.
ubiquitous_language.Verdict: Authorized evaluation of specified definition/evidence revisions.
ubiquitous_language.UNVERIFIED: Insufficient or mismatched proof, not false or numeric zero.

ports: EvidenceRepository.put(record) -> EvidenceRef; get(ref, access_scope) -> typed record; records use a discriminated Definition/Observation/Verdict union.

EvidenceAdmission.validate(record, authority_snapshot) -> Admissible | Rejected. Definition requires issuer/ref; Observation requires method, input refs, observed value and uncertainty; Verdict requires definition refs, observation refs, evaluator identity/authority, policy revision and outcome.
ExecutionVerdict bridge passes only validated definition/observation values to existing evaluate_verdict; generic evidence records cannot directly transition lifecycle.
adapters: Proposed evidence_learning/adapters/local_evidence_repository.py implements immutable content-addressed local files and sanitized export.

Proposed execution_coordination/adapters/evidence_verdict_bridge.py translates neutral typed records to existing EvidenceDefinition/Observation and leaves evaluate_verdict semantics owned by execution_coordination.
contracts.state: Immutable schema_version=1 record envelope: kind, project/profile, logical ID, revision, source refs, authority refs where applicable, payload, access label, preceding/superseded refs. Operational applicability/hold pointers are separate from the evidence body.
transitions: New record -> structurally validated -> authority/link validated -> admissible typed record.
Observation conflict appends competing record and marks impacted applicability held; never overwrites a definition.
Verdict with mismatched revision or missing evidence remains UNVERIFIED/refused at acceptance. Authorized supersession appends links.
contracts.identities: EvidenceRef uses SHA-256 of canonical envelope without self-digest. Logical IDs persist across revisions; source observations retain original invocation/event identity. No role conversion by changing a label on the same digest.
contracts.persistence: Use the existing execution_coordination.ports.operational_store.OperationalStore, backed by SQLiteOperationalStore; profile-scoped aggregates and expected-version commit. Immutable artifact bodies use the shared EvidenceRepository described in shared_contracts, outside the repository. No new database engine or distributed queue. Long-lived evidence is a separate content-addressed filesystem repository, not operational state or learned policy. Referenced evidence is retained; no automatic deletion in this wave.
contracts.concurrency: Reads return a version; each mutation supplies expected_version. SQLite transactions serialize commits; VersionConflict returns a typed stale-input hold, with no blind retry of a decision. Duplicate identity with identical digest is a no-op; different digest is a conflict. Never hold a SQLite transaction across filesystem, provider or network calls. Concurrent identical put is idempotent; different bytes cannot overwrite a content-addressed object.
failure_modes: Observation submitted as Definition without normative authority -> reject.
Missing artifact/hash mismatch -> UNVERIFIED and no PASS.
Unknown numeric observation -> null plus reason, never zero.
contracts.recovery: Validate object digest on read; rehydrate operational pointers from retained objects and receipt history. Missing evidence requires recovery from exact pinned source or fresh observation, never reconstruction of a measurement by inference.
contracts.evidence: Retain role, exact definition/evidence/policy links, observations in source sequence, conflicts, rejection reasons and evaluator authorization.
contracts.observability: evidence.admitted/rejected and verdict.inapplicable use typed record IDs/reasons; no secret content or private reasoning in logs.
contracts.security: Evidence is inert untrusted data. Role and issuer validated against authority snapshot; export redacts a derived object retaining its parent ref. Immutable raw private records remain access-controlled locally.
contracts.operator_surface: Proposed evidence show/trace/export prints role and provenance chain explicitly; status never collapses observation into verdict.

specified: A new lifecycle, autonomous policy promotion or private chain-of-thought storage.
non_goals.phase_interpretation: Phase-relative exclusions in Phase 8 mean no design authored during SPECIFY; this Phase 9 authors design only. No implementation, BIUs, verification verdict or operational adoption is performed.

contracts.architecture_fitness: Keep domain values and ports vendor-neutral; domain/application may not import adapters. Terminal outcome, objective/authority change, contradiction, stale vector, exhausted context/age/transition/block limit, provider replacement or explicit end -> ENDED; renewal always new episode/epoch and fresh context.

contracts.concurrency: Reads return a version; each mutation supplies expected_version. SQLite transactions serialize commits; VersionConflict returns a typed stale-input hold, with no blind retry of a decision. Duplicate identity with identical digest is a no-op; different digest is a conflict. Never hold a SQLite transaction across filesystem, provider or network calls. Serialize authority-bearing episode commands under an objective reservation; validate epoch and entire relevant state vector while holding that reservation through durable command-intent commit. All relevant kernel writers honor the same reservation/CAS protocol. Release before external effects; effects revalidate fence. Multiple monitors dedupe attention with stable key.

design_decisions: Default tenure policy: one BIU, maximum age 3600 seconds, maximum 32 admitted transitions, maximum blocked duration 300 seconds, accepted contradiction count 1, any relevant state-vector mismatch ends tenure. Default context-usage source is UNBOUND and its numeric threshold is disabled; absence of a binding alone does not terminate every episode. All other tenure limits remain active. If explicitly BOUND, threshold is 0.8 and reaching it ends tenure; unavailable, stale, wrong-invocation or invalid measurements terminate conservatively. Monotonic clock within process; persisted UTC deadline for restart; clock regression holds. Values are versioned composition policy, not authority or increased budget. The 3600 seconds is a proposed configurable design default, not a claim that the bootstrap waiter timeout or historical values are canonical; no empirical derivation or inheritance is asserted.
Terminal/objective/authority/provider/model changes and explicit request end immediately. Reaching any limit ends, never silently renews; authorized begin of new epoch retains budget accounting.

SF-REQ-008 durability elaboration and SF-REQ-029 provider normalization amendments are excluded. Existing store versions/events suffice; no promise of normalized provider telemetry. POSTW1-DECIDE-006A gates actual bootstrap handoff.

Tenure checks run on each result/event and an injected deadline timer independent of the model. Epoch expiry prevents new authority-bearing commands but does not fabricate cancellation of already-admitted workers. Relevant authority/source changes advance a durable applicability revision observed by guarded admission; an external source whose freshness cannot be checked causes a hold. For a BOUND context-usage source only, unknown usage is conservative termination; UNBOUND is explicitly recorded and never represented as zero usage or measured-safe context.

Context observation validity is decidable: matching current invocation, finite used >= 0, finite limit > 0, and sample from the current tenure check (request correlation must match); unavailable or prior-check samples end tenure when BOUND. Compare used/limit >= 0.8; no normalization or estimated values. Default UNBOUND policy does not claim telemetry-based context safety. Explicit context-exhausted operator/provider events still end tenure; neither they nor the optional fixture close LRN-023.

Contradiction is a judgment obligation owned by the authorized episode operator under the episode authority, not an inferred semantic predicate. The operator names conflicting authoritative facts/actions and records rationale and evidence refs. Mechanically count only AcceptedContradiction for the current episode/epoch/vector with authorized actor and nonempty resolvable conflicting_refs/rationale; one ends tenure. Invalid, stale or unauthorized reports produce InvalidJudgment and cannot act as authoritative termination input. Truth of the contradiction requires operator judgment; fixture automation proves admission and termination, not semantic truth.

contracts.state: Per active factory aggregate retain lifecycle-entry UTC time/revision, expected effect kind and generation, stable effect identity, reservation owner/fence, invocation correlation, pending/completed/unknown effect status, durable outcome/evidence ref and suppression/resolution ref. transitions: IMPLEMENT -> expects producer; VERIFY -> verifier; ACCEPT -> each required outstanding closure effect; REVIEW, terminal or ACCEPT with no outstanding closure -> no launch recovery.
Age < G -> NO_ACTION; age >= G and complete absence proof -> GAP. Active/pending/correlated completed/unknown effect -> no new launch; unknown -> hold/readback.

Judgment outcome -> durable suppression/attention regardless of age. Seen-only receipt leaves suppression. Valid matching resolution or newer same-lane correlated nonjudgment outcome permits reinspection, never unconditional retry.
Authorized gap -> reserve -> re-read evidence/admission -> durable intent -> fenced dispatch -> receipt/readback -> normal kernel projection.
contracts.identities: Canonical effect key is hash(profile, persisted repository/project identity, BIU identity, contract digest, lifecycle-entry generation, role/closure-action key). contracts.persistence: Use the existing execution_coordination.ports.operational_store.OperationalStore, backed by SQLiteOperationalStore; profile-scoped aggregates and expected-version commit. contracts.concurrency: Multiple reconciler processes and delayed original deliveries contend on the same durable lane reservation/effect key. Fence must be checked by the launch/closure consumer under the same durable ownership boundary immediately before side effect. No check-then-await-in-memory guarantee. Ambiguous already-sent effects never acquire a fresh identity or auto-retry.

The Wave 1 impossible-isolation pattern is correctly replaced by four observables, but SF-REQ-053-AC-02 demands a fixture for every SWF-27 termination cause while the design gives 'contradiction' a threshold of 1 with no decidable predicate or observation source.

Deny-network offline fixtures, inert imported prose, access-labelled evidence, redacted export, and re-checked authority/custody/fence at dispatch; no capability is assumed that the existing code contradicts.

Unknown effects read back first, no unfenced takeover or lease expiry, ambiguity parks, UNKNOWN never becomes zero, and the design explicitly refuses to promise finite successful recovery when the store is unavailable.

17 opportunities, each with a proven-red obligation; the 7 reused promotions keep the ADVISORY/BLOCKING strengths the Gap Trap backlog assigned them (LRN-003, LRN-010, LRN-019 advisory; LRN-001/002/004/016 blocking).

Two stated safety properties have no probe: 015's 'live profile composition must fail closed when AssessmentAuthority is unbound', and 053's tenure threshold, whose fixture passes on injected values while no composition binds a real source.
Every contract is exercisable offline against a real temporary SQLite store, local bare Git remote and fake clock, with no provider credentials or network.

Ports, state, transitions and identities are concrete enough to decompose, but 013 cannot be decomposed until the allocation source is settled and no contract states the context import-direction rule its own enforcement fixture would check.
All seven promotions are reused at plausible boundaries, counted honestly (8 entries / 7 unique), and none is claimed as deployed enforcement.

SF-REQ-051-AC-04 plus failure_modes 'Mechanically consistent impossible capability premise -> review rejection' and 014's PremiseEvidence port; residual risk is that premise evidence comes from the same installation doctor that produced the 17/17 false assurance, and LRN-014 was deliberately not promoted.

SF-REQ-014 design_decisions pin four observables (positive access, profile scoping, rejected out-of-scope request, unchanged outside-state readback) and refuse credential-denial oracles; SF-REQ-014-AC-03 traces it.

shared_contracts.interfaces_and_wiring_proof binds every public composed operation to an intact-success and typed-failure probe against a real temporary SQLite store, with LRN-002 instantiated in 014-composition and 039-composed-lifecycle; residual is that eight contracts carry no contract-level composed-path entry.

SF-REQ-014 transitions gate DRAFT -> FEASIBLE_PLAN before 013 compilation consumes proof_plan, and 014-repair-preservation reuses LRN-004 as BLOCKING; the ordering diagnostic itself stays ADVISORY, matching the promotion decision.

039's OutcomeEvidencePort/RoleOutcomeRecord ('Missing RoleOutcomeRecord holds even when WorkerOutcome.kind is success'), 015's 'Zero exit without semantic result -> failure, not readiness', and 016's verdict admission rules; see DV-1 for who owns supplying it.

findings.finding: SF-REQ-039's design does not merely add an offline harness: it changes the shared execution kernel. It requires role-by-role orchestration replacing FactoryCoordinator._completed_for_outcome, a composed role router, and a new OutcomeEvidencePort whose absence blocks a transition even on WorkerOutcome.kind == 'success'. That application is composed by the live paths (sandbox_run_profile.py:308, github_profile.py:33) with RealWorkerProvider, and no contract assigns anyone to produce RoleOutcomeRecord on the non-scripted path; invocation_runtime is not a bounded context owned by any of the ten. The authorizing party is named only as 'when authorized', and shared_contracts.authority_boundaries simultaneously forbids 'current worker/lifecycle contract edits'.
findings.why_it_matters: A production capability is being introduced inside a test-proof requirement with no owner and no live-path probe. Offline scenarios would pass while the sandbox profile holds on every producer success, and the capability gap would surface at Agent-Ready or live proof — the exact shape of the Wave 1 unowned live transport.
findings.suggested_repair: Name the requirement and owner for canonical multi-role orchestration and for RoleOutcomeRecord emission on the real worker path (or record it as an explicit authority gap returned to SPECIFY); reconcile that against shared_contracts.authority_boundaries; and state the behaviour of the live profile when the sidecar is unavailable before the change lands.

findings.finding: The contract makes an externally supplied 'authorized allocation' a mandatory input carrying unit_key, BIU identity, obligation extents, capabilities, budgets, dependency edges and closure duties — effectively the whole BIU — and holds when it is absent ('Missing allocation meaning is a planning hold, never guessed'). Neither the canonical definition ('Lower governed requirements into bounded BIUs with explicit requirement-satisfaction links and dependency DAGs') nor the Phase 8 specification's scope, dependencies or authority_gaps mentions such an input or an actor who produces it. No authority gap is recorded for it, in contrast to the careful G1/G2 treatment in SF-REQ-015.
findings.why_it_matters: This silently narrows a P1 requirement from 'compile requirements into BIUs' to 'validate a hand-authored allocation', and leaves the Wave 2A outcome dependent on an unowned upstream step. Whether the decomposition author is in Wave 2 scope is a product-owner question, and the design's own rule (SF-REQ-051: an uncovered authority question returns to SPECIFY) says it should not have been settled here.
findings.suggested_repair: Record the allocation source as an explicit authority gap on SF-REQ-013 and return the question to SPECIFY: either name the owner and interface that produces allocations, or re-specify SF-REQ-013 to derive the decomposition under stated constraints.

findings.finding: Enforcement opportunity 051-architecture-boundary proposes extending the fitness suite with a 'context import-direction/port compatibility fixture', but no contract states the permitted direction graph. The existing checker (tools/fitness/check_architecture.py, CHECKS = layering, vendor-signature, port-contract, configuration, determinism) has no context-level rule, and the design itself creates coupling in both directions (context_assembly adapters bind execution_coordination ports and evidence_learning ports; execution_coordination's 015 consumes context_assembly DesignApplicability; 014's premise adapter reads installation and composition/doctor_probes). deferred_to_implementation is empty in all ten contracts, so nothing signals that this is open.
findings.why_it_matters: The implementer must invent the rule the deterministic check enforces, which the architecture authority forbids ('No agent may invent repository structure merely because implementation starts') and which the bounded-context model was supposed to settle first. A fixture written against an invented direction graph is a gate that certifies the implementer's own assumption.
findings.suggested_repair: State the allowed context dependency direction (including whether execution_coordination may depend on context_assembly types and how evidence_learning adapters may reach installation/composition) as a fixed decision in shared_contracts, then define 051-architecture-boundary against it.

findings.finding: The inventory must recognise requirement identifiers inside three prose forms, yet no contract field pins the identifier grammar. ubiquitous_language says only 'Existing SF-REQ identifier, never generated from wording'; identities says the ID is 'the supplied SF-REQ ID scoped to the source project'; failure_modes covers heading-only omission, conflicts, digest mismatch and retired-ID reuse but not an unrecognised identifier shape. The 011-inventory fixture pins counts (56/53) over a baseline whose IDs are all plain three-digit forms, and no probe uses a suffixed or extended identifier.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the PY-09B failure verbatim, one layer up: an implementer writes SF-REQ-\d{3}, a later authorized identifier with a suffix or a different project prefix is silently dropped, the counts fixture still passes, and the register under-reports definitions — the precise omission SF-REQ-011 exists to prevent. Wave 1's version also reported the wrong reason, which is why an unrecognised shape needs a typed outcome rather than absence.
findings.suggested_repair: Fix the recognised identifier grammar as an explicit design decision, require an unrecognised identifier shape to yield a typed UNVERIFIED/conflict record rather than an omission, and add a non-conforming-identifier fixture with a proven-red obligation to 011-inventory.

findings.finding: The composition section states 'Live profile composition must fail closed when AssessmentAuthority is unbound' and failure_modes lists 'No configured assessment contract or ownership -> hold', but neither appears in any acceptance_design_trace (AC-01..AC-05 cover lint, dispositions, fingerprint staleness, envelope parity and PY-10 replay) and the single enforcement opportunity 015-envelope-applicability covers only parsing and handling. LRN-002 is not reused here.
findings.why_it_matters: The unbound-authority path is the one place a recurrence of the unowned-transport failure would be caught, and it is the only stated safety property in this contract that nothing probes. The global wiring obligation in shared_contracts covers it in principle, but nothing tracks it as an enforcement item.
findings.suggested_repair: Add an LRN-002 composed-path entry to SF-REQ-015 asserting that the live profile refuses to construct, or returns OWNER_ASSIGNMENT_HOLD, when AssessmentAuthority is unbound, with a proven-red obligation that binding a stub makes it fail.

findings.finding: The default tenure policy includes 'context usage threshold 0.8 of the invocation limit', with 'Missing context usage/limit ends tenure conservatively', while SF-REQ-029 provider normalization is explicitly excluded and no port or adapter in the contract supplies context usage or the invocation limit. LRN-023 (provider-progress-observability) remains an unfilled capability gap.
findings.why_it_matters: In the real composition there is no source for this input, so either every episode ends at its first tenure check or the threshold is inert — while the AC-02 boundary fixture passes on injected values. That is a probe that cannot see the condition that will actually hold in production.
findings.suggested_repair: Either name the port that observes context usage and its unavailable case, or drop the threshold from the default policy and state that conservative termination applies only when a bound source reports an unusable value; add a fixture for the 'no source bound at all' composition.

findings.finding: 'contradiction count 1' is given as a tenure limit, but no contract field defines what a contradiction is, what observes it, or from which input it is derived — unlike the state-vector mismatch and numeric limits, which are decidable. SF-REQ-053-AC-02 nevertheless requires a policy fixture for every SWF-27 termination cause, and 053-tenure-fence is BLOCKING on 'every named termination cause'.
findings.why_it_matters: A BLOCKING gate with one undecidable member will either be implemented against an invented predicate or quietly dropped from the battery; both outcomes are the 'gate that cannot run' pattern Wave 1 recorded.
findings.suggested_repair: Define the contradiction predicate and its observation source, or mark that cause as a judgment obligation with a named actor in the way SF-REQ-014 handles non-mechanical predicates.

findings.finding: The G+I detection bound is honestly caveated as holding only 'with progressing clock, complete evidence and functioning scans', and 053 asserts 'Persistent monitor lifetime is independent of model invocation', but no contract names who hosts or supervises the monitor and periodic scan, and no non-goal excludes it.
findings.why_it_matters: Wave 1 lost an untracked background watcher launched with '&' and separately misread a systemd-managed process as not running. An unhosted scanner turns 056 into a capability whose failure mode is indistinguishable from quiet, which is the class the coordinator's own assessment singled out as most dangerous.
findings.suggested_repair: Name the owner of monitor hosting and supervision (or record it as an explicit out-of-scope gap with the actor who will close it), and require the scan to expose a liveness observation of itself rather than only of the work it inspects.

bootstrap_assumptions_found: No bootstrap machinery is adopted as architecture: the session-bound waiter is replaced by a monitor whose lifetime is independent of model invocation with activation unbound by default, the file mailbox is deliberately kept as a separate operator duty with a distinct namespace and only a read-only migration-staging adapter, and the resident multi-BIU tenure is explicitly refused in favour of a one-BIU default.

Weak candidate only: the 3600 s maximum episode age coincides with the bootstrap waiter's 3600 s timeout and carries no provenance statement, while SF-REQ-056 explicitly disclaims its analogous 300 s ('not a claim that historical bootstrap 5 minutes is a canonical invariant'). The asymmetry is worth labelling; I did not establish that the value was copied.
Provider replacement as a tenure termination cause traces to SWF-27 in the specification, not to the one-off recovery authorization, and SF-REQ-029 telemetry normalization is explicitly excluded.
clean_areas: Atomic fencing and recovery semantics (shared_contracts.atomic_fencing_extension plus SF-REQ-056 concurrency/recovery) — reservation held through send and readback, no lease expiry or unfenced takeover, sorted lock order, ambiguity parks, and an explicit refusal to promise finite successful recovery.
Requirement and acceptance coverage is exact: 10/10 selected requirements, 53/53 acceptance IDs listed and traced with matching identifiers, no invented ACs and no dropped ones.

SF-REQ-014's isolation design retires the Wave 1 impossible premise properly, replacing credential denial with four observables and routing infeasible premises back to source authority rather than waiving them.
SF-REQ-015 carries the G1/G2 ownership gaps forward without filling them: no stub READY, no invented serialization contract, explicit OWNER_ASSIGNMENT_HOLD.

SF-REQ-016's role separation is concrete and enforceable — discriminated union, evaluator/policy/revision links required for a verdict, content-addressed immutability, and null-plus-reason instead of zero for unknown measurements.

The design reads the existing code accurately rather than assuming it: it correctly identifies FactoryCoordinator._completed_for_outcome as collapsing verify/review/accept/close, and correctly states that commit_with_effect/claim_effect do not validate a passed reservation fence.

The 053/056 dependency cycle is answered rather than deferred: 053 exposes AttentionPort independently, and 056 ratification is required only for 056-specific recovery, not for generic attention or tenure.

Enforcement strengths are honest — 17 opportunities all marked DESIGNED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, advisory/blocking assignments match the Gap Trap backlog decisions, and the promotion counting (8 entries, 7 unique) is stated and correct.
content.verifier_note: Read-only and pre-implementation: three of the five named contexts (context_assembly, evidence_learning, control_plane beyond decisions/CLI) are empty package skeletons, so none of the 17 designed probes exists or could be executed, and I neither re-ran the design/Wave 1 checkers nor recomputed the 28 recorded source digests; platform behaviours the design depends on — SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE fencing under real multi-process contention, deny-network CI, live worker readback durability, and provider context-usage telemetry — were reasoned about against the source, not tested.

findings_status.evidence: The kernel change is no longer authorized inside the test-proof requirement. Two SPECIFY gaps are recorded with resolution actors and explicit blocks (authority_gaps R1-GAP-039-ORCHESTRATION, R1-GAP-039-REAL-OUTCOME, each stating 'Implementers and this designer may not close it'); OutcomeEvidencePort is demoted to 'Conditional target only after R1-GAP-039-ORCHESTRATION and R1-GAP-039-REAL-OUTCOME are resolved'; composition states the separate-role path is blocked and that 'full multi-role acceptance is blocked, not passed by a parallel mock'; design_decisions[0] forbids replacing FactoryCoordinator._completed_for_outcome under SF-REQ-039 alone, reconciling with shared_contracts.authority_boundaries, which now names both gaps as blocking. The live-path hole is closed in the direction the finding demanded: the sandbox/github constructors must return ROLE_OUTCOME_BINDING_HOLD 'before any worker launch, not after every producer success', with 'Existing unmodified profiles are not claimed to enforce this future gate', and 039-composed-lifecycle adds a real-path probe whose proven_red_obligation independently kills the pre-launch binding gate and real-worker record emission. AC-01's probe is explicitly marked blocked rather than claimed satisfiable, and authority_status is downgraded to DESIGN_CANDIDATE_WITH_SPECIFY_HOLD. requirements_created=0 verified: no new Product Requirement is invented to close it.

The wrong design is withdrawn, not merely annotated. ubiquitous_language redefines Allocation as 'Derived obligation-to-unit extent mapping in a compilation candidate; not an authorized mandatory hand-authored input'; ports mark the allocation representation as 'output/internal, not prerequisite input'; design_decisions[0] states 'Supersedes the mandatory external-allocation design choice... SF-REQ-013 must derive initial decomposition from requirements/design' and 'A validator-only implementation does not satisfy this requirement'; shared_contracts.alternatives_and_selection records the withdrawal. The validator-only path is actively foreclosed, not just deprecated: transitions say 'validation of a hand-authored candidate cannot count as initial compilation acceptance', AC-02's probe says 'Hand-authored allocation fixture success is validation-only, never proof of compilation', and 013-graph-coverage's proven_red_obligation requires 'Bypass the authority-gap gate with a complete hand-authored allocation and require the no-candidate assertion to fail'. The residual product question (derive vs. named external producer, plus identity constraints) is returned as R1-GAP-013-ALLOCATION with derivation selected on stated evidence, which is exactly what the repair instruction permitted. Consequence disclosed rather than hidden: with the gap open compile returns AUTHORITY_GAP_HOLD, so 013 is now blocked rather than narrowed, and authority_status/blocks say so.

The missing rule now exists and the fixture is written against it: shared_contracts.context_dependency_direction states an explicit allowed_edges table, target_layers (cross-context imports target domain values or ports only), typed_cycles (execution_coordination MAY reference context_assembly.domain DesignApplicability; reciprocal leaf references, no module cycles) and premise_bridge (evidence_learning adapters MUST NOT import installation or composition; composition/upstream_profile owns the doctor bridge), and 051-architecture-boundary now says it 'Enforce[s] shared_contracts.context_dependency_direction exactly' with named negative fixtures (execution_coordination -> context_assembly.application, evidence_learning -> installation, evidence_learning -> composition, reciprocal leaf cycle) and positive controls. SF-REQ-014's adapters were rewritten to match the premise bridge, so the internal inconsistency the finding cited is gone. What is not closed is the invention the finding was really about: the stated table contradicts imports that exist in the repository today and supplies no exemption, baseline or scope predicate a static checker can apply, so the implementer must still invent the in-scope rule before the BLOCKING gate can run. See DV2-1 for the exact imports.

SF-REQ-011 gains an identifier_contract section that pins the grammar as a full-token regex (\A[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*)*-REQ-[0-9]{3,}(?:[A-Z])?\Z), states extraction ('capture the entire identifier slot before grammar validation', trim only outer delimiters, 'No substring match may salvage a conforming prefix from a nonconforming token'), and defines typed outcomes: IdentifierShapeConflict(status=UNVERIFIED, reason=UNRECOGNIZED_REQUIREMENT_ID, raw_token, source_ref, locator, grammar_revision=1), distinct MISSING_/AMBIGUOUS_REQUIREMENT_ID and a separate UNAUTHORIZED_REQUIREMENT_NAMESPACE, with 'they count as issues, never silently absent definitions' and recognition explicitly conferring no authority. The PY-09B mechanism is killed by a probe, not a sentence: 011-inventory now requires synthetic SF-REQ-011A / SF-REQ-1000 / TEAM-X-REQ-011 retention and typed rejection of SF-REQ-01 / SF-REQ-011AA / SF-REQ-011-extra in all three prose forms, and its proven_red_obligation is 'Replace full-token grammar with SF-REQ-[0-9]{3}, strip a suffix, or silently drop a malformed token separately: exact identity/typed-reason assertions fail even if baseline 56/53 counts pass' — i.e. the counts fixture can no longer mask the omission. I checked the grammar against the real definition corpus (docs/decisions/alienintent-software-factory-plan.md plus the Canonical-requirement/Recorded-as decision records): 134 conforming tokens, zero nonconforming, so the pinned grammar does not reject any authorized identifier in the sources it is meant to parse. Residual risk in a different corpus is DV2-2, not a failure of the grammar itself.

episode_age_3600.evidence: SF-REQ-053 design_decisions[0] (docs/evidence/wave2-design-contracts.json:1487, mirrored at docs/evidence/wave2-design-contracts.md:408) now ends: 'The 3600 seconds is a proposed configurable design default, not a claim that the bootstrap waiter timeout or historical values are canonical; no empirical derivation or inheritance is asserted.' This is the same form as SF-REQ-056's 300 s disclaimer ('not a claim that historical bootstrap 5 minutes is a canonical invariant'), so the asymmetry the verdict flagged is removed. No provenance is claimed, and none is implied — the value stays versioned composition policy, 'not authority or increased budget'.

regression.detail: The mechanical properties that previously passed are intact, and I verified them rather than trusting the repair's own numbers: 10/10 contracts, 53/53 acceptance IDs unchanged, deferred_to_implementation empty in all ten, no new bounded context, 18 enforcement opportunities with exactly one added entry (015-composed-authority, the DV-5 repair) and none removed, 9 promotion entries over 7 unique promotions, and every reused promotion keeps its prior strength (LRN-001/002/004/016 BLOCKING; LRN-003/010/019 ADVISORY) — so shared_contracts.enforcement_counting and validation.additional_checks are honest, and the previously-PASS deterministic-enforcement and coverage checks are not weakened. The .md companion was regenerated consistently (it carries the four gaps, the edge table, the identifier contract and the 3600 s disclaimer; no stale mandatory-allocation text). Two things the repair itself introduced do not hold up. (1) The new fixed edge table forbids cross-context edges that exist in production code today, and the enforcement entry that checks it has no exemption mechanism (DV2-1) — notably it forbids installation/application/doctor.py's import, and that module is the very callable the new premise_bridge routes through. (2) The new unconditional token ledger plus blocking identifier-issue semantics has no category for requirement-scoped acceptance identifiers or compound prose references (DV2-2). Both are defects of the repaired sections, not pre-existing. Separately, and not material: identifier_contract.biu_distinction calls the BIU grammar 'Existing', while its source (docs/evidence/wave1-biu-split-replan-design.json:19) calls it a proposed identity grammar and no such validator exists in src/alienintent.

new_material_findings.finding: shared_contracts.context_dependency_direction.allowed_edges forbids four import edges that the repository already contains, and 051-architecture-boundary is BLOCKING on checking 'this exact edge table' with no exemption list, baseline or scope predicate. The table gives installation an empty allow-list and omits execution_coordination -> installation and execution_coordination -> invocation_runtime, but /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/src/alienintent/execution_coordination/adapters/github_projects_v2.py:20-21 and /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/src/alienintent/execution_coordination/adapters/github_repository_api.py:14 import alienintent.installation.domain/ports, /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/src/alienintent/execution_coordination/application/local_artifact_custody.py:11 imports alienintent.invocation_runtime.domain.runtime, and /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/src/alienintent/installation/application/doctor.py:10 imports alienintent.execution_coordination.domain.webhook_authenticity. The scope sentence ('Fixed rule for all new/changed Wave 2 Python imports... Existing imports outside this slice are not retroactively certified') is not a predicate a static checker can evaluate: /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/tools/fitness/check_architecture.py walks every .py under --root (python_files/rglob in run()) and has no per-file or grandfathered-edge mechanism.
new_material_findings.why_it_matters: The implementer cannot land the BLOCKING fixture as specified. They must either edit four production modules (including local_artifact_custody.py, which SF-REQ-039 reuses, and doctor.py, which the new premise_bridge depends on) although shared_contracts.authority_boundaries forbids retroactive Wave 1 changes, or invent an exemption/scope rule the design does not state — which is DV-3's original defect displaced one step: a gate certifying the implementer's own assumption about which files the rule covers. The alternative outcome is the 'gate that cannot run' pattern: the check is quietly dropped from the suite. Repair is cheap and stays inside design authority: record the four existing edges as explicitly named, dated exceptions (or add the edges to the table with a target-layer restriction) and state whether the fixture applies repository-wide or to an enumerated module set.

new_material_findings.finding: identifier_contract.extraction requires ledgering 'every whitespace-delimited token containing -REQ- in source text', typed_failure makes every nonconforming token an IdentifierShapeConflict that 'block[s] dependent source compilation until explicitly resolved', and no substring may 'salvage a conforming prefix from a nonconforming token' — but the grammar recognises only requirement identifiers, and biu_distinction handles only the requirement/BIU pair. There is no category for requirement-scoped acceptance identifiers or compound references, both of which occur in the project's own decision and specification prose: SF-REQ-053-AC-02 and the other 52 acceptance IDs (used by this very design's acceptance_design_trace and by SF-REQ-013's obligation coverage) appear throughout /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/docs/evidence/wave2-specified-requirements.md, and compound forms appear at /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/docs/decisions/2026-09-19-software-factory-wave1-founder-decisions.md:46 ('SF-REQ-001–010'), /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/docs/decisions/2026-09-20-wave1-release-coordinator.md:83 ('SF-REQ-001/SF-REQ-002') and /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/docs/decisions/2026-09-20-candidate-worktree-retention.md:61 ('SF-REQ-030/054'). All fail the pinned regex.
new_material_findings.why_it_matters: Whenever a pinned manifest includes such a source, the inventory produces UNRECOGNIZED_REQUIREMENT_ID issues for legitimate identifiers and blocks compilation for that source, or the implementer invents an AC-suffix rule and a separator-splitting rule that extraction explicitly forbids — reintroducing the unpinned-grammar judgment DV-4 was meant to remove, now on the reject side instead of the drop side. It also collides with the retained 56/53 baseline if any baseline reference is a compound token. The known definition corpus (factory plan and Canonical-requirement/Recorded-as records) is clean, so this is a completeness defect in the new section rather than a certain failure; repair is to state the acceptance-identifier form and its typed disposition, and either exempt multi-reference tokens with an explicit separator rule or state that they are references, not identifier issues.

reverification_r1.verifier_note: Read-only, pre-implementation, and narrow by instruction: I checked the four findings, the 3600 s value and repair-induced damage, and did not re-run the other eleven checks or re-derive the design from the Phase 8 specification. None of the 18 designed probes exists or could be executed — /mnt/d/Projects/alienintent/src/alienintent/context_assembly and .../evidence_learning contain only __init__.py skeletons and control_plane has only the decision inbox/CLI — so every closure above is a judgment about design text and its stated proven-red obligations, not observed behaviour. I did not re-run tools/evidence/check_design_contracts.py or check_wave1.py, and I did not recompute the 28/29 preserved-source digests or the verdict_sha256; I verified the repair's structural counts (10 contracts, 53 ACs, 18 opportunities, 9/7 promotions, 0 deferred, one added enforcement entry) independently from the JSON and from git diff against HEAD. For DV-4 I tested the pinned regex mechanically against every -REQ- token in the factory plan and the Canonical-requirement/Recorded-as decision records (zero nonconforming) and across docs/ generally (104 distinct nonconforming, dominated by acceptance IDs), which is the basis for DV2-2's scoping; I could not establish which documents the historical 56-referenced/53-defined baseline manifest actually pins, because no manifest artifact is named in the contract. For DV2-1 I confirmed the four offending imports and the checker's whole-tree walk by reading the files, but I did not attempt to implement the proposed context-edge check, so I cannot say how many further violations a full implementation (including re-exports and TYPE_CHECKING imports, which the design requires it to inspect) would surface. Platform behaviours the design still rests on — SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE fencing under real multi-process contention, deny-network CI, live worker readback durability — were not tested. Whether the designer holds authority to fix the context edge table at all, given that the architecture authority lists the bounded-context model as unfinished pre-Python work, is an owner question I did not attempt to settle; the repair instruction directed that the graph be stated here.

reverification_r2.verifier_note: Read-only, pre-implementation, and narrow by instruction: I checked DV2-1, DV2-2, DV-3, regression, and that DV-1/DV-2/DV-4 were not reopened. I did not re-derive the design from the Phase 8 specification, did not re-audit the eleven original checks or the six advisory findings (DV-5..DV-8 were only spot-checked for survival), and did not recompute the 28 preserved-source digests or run tools/evidence/check_wave1.py, so validation.wave1_check (1075 checks, 13/13 negative controls) is unverified by me. None of the 18 designed probes exists or could be executed — src/alienintent/context_assembly and src/alienintent/evidence_learning contain only skeletons — so every closure above is a judgement about design text plus mechanically checkable facts about the repository, not observed probe behaviour. Three things I checked and deliberately did not raise as findings. (1) premise_bridge still states a normative 'evidence_learning adapters MUST NOT import installation or composition' while edge authority is gapped; I judged this in-scope for the designer because it constrains only modules this design proposes to build (evidence_learning has no imports today), it disclaims authority in its own text, and its fixtures sit in the blocked conditional_probes list rather than in any runnable BLOCKING gate. (2) token_kinds.compound_reference and .possessive_reference are specified in precise prose rather than as pinned regexes, unlike the requirement and acceptance grammars; I was able to implement them unambiguously enough to reproduce the expected 56-ID set exactly, so I do not consider this an unpinned-grammar recurrence, though a pinned pattern would be stronger. (3) biu_distinction's R1 overclaim ('Existing' BIU grammar) is corrected to 'Wave 1 proposed... not an implemented validator'. I could not verify the claim that a full directional check would surface no further violations beyond the four named, because no such checker exists and I did not write one; my AST scan covers absolute alienintent imports and relative imports across groups but not dynamic imports, importlib, or string-based module references. Platform behaviours the design still rests on — SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE fencing under real multi-process contention, deny-network CI, live worker readback durability, provider context-usage telemetry — were reasoned about, not tested. Finally: this design is verified as repaired, not as implementation-ready. Five authority gaps remain open and the artifact says so itself.

shared_contracts.canonical_encoding: Canonical digest encoding follows BiuContract: UTF-8 JSON, sorted object keys, compact separators; set-valued collections sorted, sequence-valued collections retain order, no NaN/Infinity. Use sha256:<hex>. Raw external evidence also retains a separate exact-byte digest. UUIDs for attempts/episodes are allocated once at ingress and persisted before dispatch; clock/ID creation only at injected composition boundaries.
shared_contracts.evidence_storage: EvidenceRepository is a port owned by evidence_learning; local adapter stores immutable objects under configured external evidence_root/objects/<sha256>. Write temporary sibling, flush/fsync, atomically install without overwrite, fsync directory, verify digest, then CAS operational reference. Crash before pointer leaves harmless unreferenced artifact; crash after pointer is read-verified. No operational commit references unwritten evidence. Distinct namespaces and access labels separate normative refs, observation bodies and verdicts. All referenced history retained in this wave; no GC/retention automation or new learned-policy store.
shared_contracts.operational_storage: Reuse SQLiteOperationalStore and existing profile-scoped versioned aggregate APIs; upstream:<kind>:<identity>, episode:<objective>, attention:<identity> are new namespaced payloads, not a new engine. schema_version in every new payload; reject incompatible version without mutation. Operational pointer writes use CAS; immutable evidence is never updated in place. Future payload migration requires explicit versioned design and is not implementer freedom.

Commands propagate nonzero failure, with held/unverified distinctly rendered.

atomic_fencing_extension.owner: execution_coordination; proposed FencedOperationalStore port extends existing OperationalStore without replacing it.
